recipes.name: Snowball Cake
ingredients_raw: 1 (18.25 ounce) package devil's food cake mix
1 (8 ounce) package PHILADELPHIA Cream Cheese, softened
1 (3.4 ounce) package JELL-O Vanilla Flavor Instant Pudding
1 (8 ounce) tub COOL WHIP Whipped Topping, thawed

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Combine cake mix, water, 3 eggs, and oil in a large bowl; beat with an electric mixer on low speed until moistened. Increase speed to medium and beat for 2 minutes. Pour batter into a 2 1/2-quart oven-proof bowl; scrape sides of the bowl and set aside.
Beat cream cheese, sugar, and remaining 1 egg in a mixing bowl until combined; spoon into center of cake batter.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean, about 1 hour 5 minutes.
Cool cake in the bowl for 10 minutes. Loosen cake from the bowl using a knife; invert onto a wire rack and let cool completely.
Meanwhile, whisk milk, pudding mix, and confectioners' sugar together in a medium bowl for 2 minutes. Stir in whipped topping. Refrigerate until ready to use.
Place cake on a serving plate. Frost with chilled pudding mixture; cover with coconut. Keep cake refrigerated.

raw_recipe.headline: Snowball Cake
raw_recipe.description: A grown-up version of the classic lunchbox treat, this snowball cake will bring back memories and the question we all had as kids: how did the cream filling get in there?

review.reviewBody: Baked this a week earlier, and for Thanksgiving. It was an extremely moist cake, and delicious! I had no trouble getting it out of the bowl--just ran a knife around the sides. However, we weren't fond of the frosting the first time, so the second one I baked I just beat a pint of heavy cream with a package of instant vanilla pudding (next time I'll use the cheesecake flavored pudding mix) until light and fluffy.

Cake was met with raves! I made the frosting recipe* & put on the coconut on the night before serving. Love a cake to mellow overnight. Not only I find it more flavorful & more homemade flavor! The only thing different: *I used in the frosting 3/4 cup milk. I love this frosting & use it all the time but find 1 cup milk is too much milk. This is a great frosting for any cake (without the coconut) for a chocolate mousse frosting using chocolate pudding or a lemon frosting too, using instant lemon pudding!

This recipe should have a disclaimer: LET COOL COMPLETELY BEFORE FLIPPING OUT OF BOWL. With that said, it was a goopy mess because I rushed it. Better yet, stick it in the fridge over night before flipping. Also, I did as another user suggested and used white chocolate pudding mix for the icing part of the recipe, and it tasted terrific.

I have made this cake a few times and is always a hit. I make a few changes. I make the cake from the recipe on the back of the Hershey coco power and substitute the cool whip for heavy whipped cream and I bake it in a bundt pan.

I like the idea of a "snowball " cake, it has a pretty presentation, but the filling, in my mind, leaves something to be desired. It is way too dense and not sweet enough. If I were to make it again, I would bake the cake without the filling, then after it is baked, I would make a very light whipped icing filling and, using a big pastry bag with a big tip, fill the dome of the cake with it (like filling donuts). Or, slice the top off the cake, scoop out some cake, fill it, replace the top and finish as recipe states.

I make it in a clean bowl too. I like to pour the cream cheese mix in first, then pour the devil's food over it. That way, the layers are clearly separate. Color the coconut green (3 tbs milk and 3 drops green coloring) to make an Easter cake!

This was a beautiful cake I served at an office potluck during the holidays by adding sliced spearmint candy and cinnamon candies to make holly decorations on it. My family doesn't like coconut so for Christmas dinner I made a white cake and used pistachio pudding for the frosting and it was a big hit. This would be a great year round recipe decorated by whatever holiday you are serving it on.
Super moist and delicious. Everyone raved. I used real whipped cream instead of cool whip. Perfect.
I made this last week and covered the top with shaved white chocolate instead of coconut and it was a HIT at my dinner party! It took about 1h15m to cook.

The cake was absolutely delicious even though the center filling didn't turn out right. However I greased the bowl I baked it in and it came out of the bowl very easy. I had company the evening I made it and everyone love it.

Turned out great! But I mixed it in one bowl and had another heat-proof bowl that was greased and floured that I poured the batter into and baked it in. No sticking at all! The filling was great! And the icing was light and not greasy at all (like some icings can be).

We used our standard chocolate cake recipe for the base and the filling/frosting from this recipe, and it turned out great! We had a lot of cake batter, so we used a 2 qt round casserole dish for most of it and put the rest in a 9-inch round cake tin. (The filling went into the casserole dish per the recipe.) To assemble, we used the cake tin for the base layer, put a layer of the frosting, and then turned the casserole out on top of it. Made a perfect dome! We also dyed the coconut and frosting pink for that authentic snoball look. Husband loved it!
I originally got this recipe from Kraft, but lost it. Was thrilled to find it here. Its a tradition in our home.....snowball cake for Christmas dessert....yummy
Didn’t taste anything like one and had to find something else for my grandma’s birthday. It’s still neat though.
This is a very easy cake to make. Personally did not care for the icing. I adjusted and used a buttercream icing.
I used homemade whipped cream and an Italian cream cheese. No pudding.

I made this for the first time 3 years ago. It is such a favorite that I now am making 1 for Thanksgiving, 3 for Christmas and last Easter I made one in the shape of an egg. Always the star at desert time.

The cake was easy to make and looked great. Friends at my dinner asked for the frosting recipe. I would make it again.
Sharon G.
